name: Habildar Rojob Ali Khan
seoTitle: Habildar Rojob Ali Khan and the Chittagong Uprising of 1857
seoDescription: Learn about Habildar Rojob Ali Khan, associated with the Chittagong sepoy uprising against East India Company rule in 1857, and the limits of the surviving record.
role: Havildar associated with the Chittagong sepoy uprising
contribution: Regional accounts identify Havildar Rojob Ali Khan, also spelled Rajab Ali Khan, with the sepoy uprising at Chittagong in November 1857. The revolt involved soldiers of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, who left Chittagong and moved toward Sylhet. The surviving scholarship gives limited biographical detail about Rojob Ali himself, so claims about his origins, precise command, and later fate remain uncertain.
context: Chittagong and eastern Bengal during the 1857 uprising against East India Company rule. The Chittagong outbreak was part of a wider rebellion, with its own local course and an ensuing movement of rebel soldiers toward Sylhet.
impact: Rojob Ali Khan is remembered in regional accounts as a leader associated with the Chittagong phase of the 1857 uprising. His profile also illustrates how local accounts preserve names and memories that are sparsely represented in broader histories; the limits of the evidence make careful attribution important.
shortAnswer: A havildar associated in regional accounts with the 1857 Chittagong sepoy uprising against East India Company rule.
